detections.evidence_quote: Vaccines as rent-seeking behavior from Big Pharma and their corporate masters
detections.summary: Guest describes vaccines, especially recurring boosters, as part of a 'rent-seeking' profit model driven by Wall Street investment funds and Big Pharma.

detections.evidence_quote: corporate masters, which are these huge investment funds that also control the media and control Big Tech
detections.summary: Guest frames vaccines and Big Pharma as part of a coordinated rent-seeking scheme involving investment funds that also control media and Big Tech.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Vaccine manufacturers and their investment-fund backers push recurring vaccines, such as boosters every six months, primarily as a profit-driven 'rent-seeking' scheme rather than for health benefit.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Vaccines as rent-seeking behavior from Big Pharma and their corporate masters
verification_candidates.rationale: This attributes a profit-driven motive to vaccine dosing schedules and industry structure; the claim about investment-fund control and rent-seeking intent is checkable against how vaccine policy and industry ownership actually work.
